title: Unit Circle Visualizer
description: Drag the angle slider to see the point (cos θ, sin θ) move on the unit circle with live sin, cos and tan.
howto: Drag the slider or type an angle from 0° to 360°.
Watch the red radius, the blue cosine and purple sine projections.
Read sin, cos, tan and the point coordinates below the circle.

faqs.q: Why is the y-axis flipped in the picture?
faqs.a: Screen coordinates grow downward, so the SVG flips the sine value — the math shown in the labels is the true (cos θ, sin θ).
At 90° and 270°, where cos θ = 0 and the tangent line would be vertical (±∞).

faqs.q: What do the dashed lines show?
faqs.a: The dashed blue segment is the cosine (adjacent / hypotenuse) and the dashed purple segment is the sine (opposite / hypotenuse) for that angle.
